title: Marginal Distributions of Multinomial Are Binomial
description: Proves that each marginal component of a multinomial distribution follows a binomial distribution, using the probability generating function (PGF) approach via the multinomial theorem.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None. All 10 theorems are fully proved with 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The fact that marginals of the multinomial distribution are binomial is a classical result in probability theory, following from the multinomial theorem and the binomial theorem. If $(X_1, \ldots, X_k) \sim \text{Multinomial}(n, p_1, \ldots, p_k)$, then each $X_i \sim \text{Binomial}(n, p_i)$. This was known implicitly since Laplace's *Théorie Analytique des Probabilités* (1812), but is rarely proved explicitly in formal mathematics because it follows so naturally from generating functions. The probability generating function $E[t^{X_i}] = (p_i t + (1-p_i))^n$ was systematized in the 20th century and provides the cleanest proof: two random variables with the same PGF must have the same distribution.
overview.problemStatement: If $(X_1, \ldots, X_k) \sim \text{Multinomial}(n, p_1, \ldots, p_k)$ with $\sum p_i = 1$, does each component $X_i$ follow $\text{Binomial}(n, p_i)$?
overview.text: Proves that the probability generating function of each marginal component $X_{i_0}$ of a multinomial distribution equals $(p_{i_0} \cdot t + (1 - p_{i_0}))^n$, which is exactly the PGF of $\text{Binomial}(n, p_{i_0})$. The proof uses the multinomial MGF theorem with a strategically chosen weight function.
overview.proofStrategy: Apply the multinomial MGF theorem with weight function $g(i) = t$ if $i = i_0$ and $g(i) = 1$ otherwise. The product $\prod g(i)^{k(i)}$ collapses to $t^{k(i_0)}$ since all other factors equal $1^{k(i)} = 1$. The weighted sum $\sum p(i) g(i) = p(i_0) t + \sum_{i \neq i_0} p(i) = p(i_0) t + (1 - p(i_0))$ using $\sum p(i) = 1$. Together these give the Binomial PGF.
keyInsights: The PGF approach is natural: choose $g(i) = t^{[i = i_0]}$ to 'select' one coordinate
The multinomial theorem IS the proof — no additional work beyond algebraic manipulation
Product concentration: $\prod_{i \in s} (\text{if } i = i_0 \text{ then } t \text{ else } 1)^{k(i)} = t^{k(i_0)}$ via `Finset.prod_eq_single`
Sum simplification: $\sum_s p(i) \cdot (\text{if } i = i_0 \text{ then } t \text{ else } 1) = p(i_0) t + (1 - p(i_0))$ via linearity and `Finset.sum_ite_eq'`

The direct PMF formula `multinomial_marginal_pmf` is proved via an explicit bijection between filtered piAntidiag elements and `(s.erase i₀).piAntidiag (n−j)`, bypassing polynomial coefficient extraction entirely

sections.title: Module Overview and Proof Strategy
sections.summary: Explains the open question (marginals of multinomial are binomial?), the PGF proof strategy (choose g(i) = t if i=i₀ else 1), and the Mathlib dependencies (Finset.sum_pow_eq_sum_piAntidiag, Finset.prod_eq_single, Finset.sum_ite_eq'). Also includes imports.

sections.title: Setup: Multinomial PMF and MGF Identity
sections.summary: Defines multinomialProb (the multinomial PMF: multinomial coefficient × product of p(i)^k(i)) and proves multinomial_mgf_real (the algebraic MGF identity: (∑ p(i)g(i))^n = ∑_k P(X=k) · ∏ g(i)^k(i)) and multinomialProb_sum_one (normalization: ∑ P(X=k) = 1 when ∑ p(i) = 1).

sections.title: Main Theorem: Marginal PGF Formula
sections.summary: Proves multinomial_marginal_pgf: the PGF of marginal X_{i₀} equals (p(i₀)·t + (1−p(i₀)))^n. Uses the MGF identity with indicator weight g(i) = t if i=i₀ else 1. Two key inline lemmas: prod_simp (product collapses to t^k(i₀)) and sum_simp (weighted sum simplifies using normalization).

sections.title: Corollaries: Binomial Identification and Normalization
sections.summary: multinomial_marginal_pgf_eq_binomial rewrites the marginal PGF as the binomial expansion ∑ C(n,j)·p^j·(1−p)^(n−j)·t^j, confirming marginals are Binomial(n, p(i₀)). multinomial_marginal_sum_one derives normalization from multinomialProb_sum_one.

sections.title: Direct PMF Formula via Bijection
sections.summary: Directly proves P(X_{i₀}=j) = C(n,j)·p(i₀)^j·(1−p(i₀))^(n−j) via an explicit bijection between filtered piAntidiag elements and (s.erase i₀).piAntidiag (n−j). Uses Finset.sum_nbij', Nat.multinomial_insert to factor the multinomial coefficient, and the multinomial theorem on the erased subset.

sections.title: Bool Case: Bernoulli Marginals
sections.summary: Instantiates the main theorem to s = {false, true} with p(true) = p, p(false) = 1−p. Proves bernoulli_marginal_pgf (true component PGF = (pt+(1−p))^n), binomial_2_pgf (n=2 special case), and bernoulli_false_marginal_pgf (false component PGF = ((1−p)t+p)^n).

conclusion.summary: The main result `multinomial_marginal_pgf` proves that the PGF of each marginal of the multinomial distribution equals the Binomial PGF. Additionally, `multinomial_marginal_pmf` directly proves the PMF formula P(X_{i₀}=j) = C(n,j)·p(i₀)^j·(1−p(i₀))^(n−j) via an explicit bijection and Nat.multinomial_insert. All 10 theorems fully machine-verified, 0 sorries.
openQuestions: Can the proof be extended to show joint independence of disjoint subsets of multinomial components?

crossReferences.description: Proves the multinomial MGF formula that this file uses as its key tool
